plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan for the Eastern Wyoming Sequestration Hub, Laramie County, Wyoming
ama_definition: The modeled free-phase CO2 plume area 50 years after injection ends plus a 0.5-mile buffer (Area #1), which is functionally the same as the MMA; one AMA for the whole project life (p31).
mma_definition: The stabilized CO2 plume extent (2 percent saturation cutoff, 50 years after end of injection) plus a 0.5-mile all-around buffer, shown on Figure 10 (p31-32).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Pipelines/surface equipment (wear at flanges, relief valves, accidents) and wellbores (injection wells, M-1 wells, three abandoned penetrations, one of which, Fritz 1, needs remedial plugging) are rated 'minor' likelihood; confining zone, seismicity, lateral migration and future drilling are rated negligible or not anticipated (p33-37).
baseline_summary: A mixed baseline: one year of pre-injection groundwater, soil gas and atmospheric sampling around each injection well, semiannual pre-injection USDW/M-1 fluid sampling and continuous M-1 pressure/temperature, existing 2D/3D seismic as the plume baseline, and historical USGS seismicity; operating parameters are also continuously monitored against set points (p39, p43-45, p54).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the RR-12 mass balance, surface leakage and vented/fugitive emissions under 98.446(f)(3); new wells or status changes noted in the annual report; inspection and test records kept available for EPA review. Class VI monitoring follows WDEQ Chapter 24 permits. No commitment to publish measurement data (p7, p33, p42-43, p47-48, p50-51).

rows.detail: Custody-transfer meter at the pipeline delivery point to each site measures mass and composition continuously; mass flow meters with daily totalizers on each of six injection wells; quarterly CO2 concentration from the gas measurement database.
rows.location: Custody-transfer point and each injection well (six sites)
rows.evidence_quote: A custody-transfer meter will be used at the CO2 source (pipeline) to continuously measure the mass and composition of CO2 received

rows.detail: Injection pressure, temperature and rate monitored continuously through a Central Control Center and SCADA; high/low set points programmed; automatic data flags; manual and automatic shutdowns installed.
rows.location: Each injection well; Central Control Center
rows.trigger_or_response: Pressure or rate outside set points: automatic flag, field personnel investigate; unresolved deviations get detailed investigation and leak quantification.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection well pressure, temperature, and injection rate will be continuously monitored.

rows.detail: Tubing and casing (annulus) pressures of injection wells monitored continuously; monitors flag pressures that statistically deviate from design, which would reveal leaks inside or outside the wellbore.
rows.trigger_or_response: Statistical deviation from design pressures flagged; identified integrity issue addressed with corrective action.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection well tubing and casing pressures will be monitored continuously.

rows.detail: MITs and pressure tests on injection wells to verify internal and external integrity, per WDEQ Chapter 24 Class VI requirements; no interval stated in the plan.
rows.trigger_or_response: Well integrity issue identified: corrective actions.
rows.evidence_quote: Injectors will also be monitored with mechanical integrity tests (MITs) and pressure tests to ensure internal and external integrity.

rows.detail: Plan refers to downhole pressure and temperature measurements indicating plume stabilization, but names no injection-zone gauges or wells; Juniper M-1 gauges were used only to characterize initial pressure gradient.
rows.evidence_quote: after downhole pressure and temperature measurements indicate that the plume has stabilized

rows.detail: Routine field inspections by trained personnel; quarterly wellhead inspections recorded on a data sheet (corrosion, bolts, seals, valves, gaskets) including pipelines within 100 feet of each injection well.
rows.location: Wellheads, valves and piping across the MMA; pipelines within 100 feet of injection wells
rows.trigger_or_response: Faults repaired; inoperable surface safety valve: well shut in immediately and valve repaired within 90 days.
rows.evidence_quote: Injection well wellheads will be inspected on a quarterly basis

rows.detail: Scheduled point-source surveys with a portable NDIR CO2 meter (GPS-logged) at injection wellheads and M-1 wells at least quarterly, other MMA locations annually; handheld pSense CO2 meter at wellhead and nearby pipelines during quarterly inspections.
rows.location: Injection wellheads, above-confining-zone wells, pipelines/delivery systems within the MMA
rows.trigger_or_response: Also triggered by eddy covariance or other anomalies; leakage quantified from leak flow rate and CO2 concentration.
rows.evidence_quote: Point-source measurement will be conducted with a portable non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) CO2 meter.

rows.detail: Semiannual soil gas flux and CO2/CH4 ratio with a portable flux accumulation chamber (LI-COR 8200-01S) and LI-7810 analyzer at baseline locations near each injection site; results compared with pre-injection baseline.
rows.location: Fixed baseline locations near each injection site (Figure 10); within 10 feet of suspect wells or buried pipelines if leakage suspected
rows.trigger_or_response: Flux or gas ratios departing from baseline, or leak indications from other monitoring, direct additional targeted soil gas surveys.
rows.evidence_quote: Soil gas composition monitoring will also be performed prior to injection to establish a baseline.

rows.detail: Three shallow USDW wells per injection pad (18 total) plus the six M-1 wells sampled for cations, anions, dissolved CO2, H2S, TDS, alkalinity, pH, conductance; semiannual before and during injection, annual in PISC.
rows.location: USDW-1/-2/-3 wells at each of six injection pads and M-1 wells
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviation from baseline assessed for leakage; leak rate quantified from increased CO2 concentration in formation fluids.
rows.evidence_quote: Any deviation from the baseline analysis will be assessed for potential indications of leakage.

rows.detail: Six M-1 wells monitoring the Sundance Formation above the confining zone with continuous pressure/temperature gauges and semiannual fluid sampling; DTS/DAS fiber installed or planned behind casing for future use.
rows.location: Juniper, Azalea, Spirea, Barberry, Old Barberry and Cypress M-1 wells (Sundance Formation)
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviation from baseline assessed as possible leakage through the confining zone.
rows.evidence_quote: Monitoring wells to directly measure pressure, temperature, and fluid composition will be dedicated to geologic sequestration.

rows.detail: Annual wireline temperature log in each injection well and annual DTS or temperature logs in the M-1 wells to check for leakage through the confining zone or along wellbores.
rows.location: All six injection wells and six M-1 monitoring wells
rows.evidence_quote: An annual temperature log via wireline will be conducted in each injection well.

rows.detail: Reliance on the public USGS Intermountain West Seismic Network during injection, with a historical seismicity review (depth, magnitude, frequency) as baseline; no site seismometers.
rows.location: Public USGS Intermountain West Seismic Network
rows.evidence_quote: High Plains will monitor the USGS Intermountain West Seismic Network for seismic events.

rows.detail: Time-lapse 2D seismic for plume tracking: existing 2D/3D surveys as baseline, one repeat survey during injection and one after plume stabilization, compared to baseline to map plume extent.
rows.location: Injection interval across the project area
rows.trigger_or_response: Used to detect lateral migration outside the modeled plume area.
rows.evidence_quote: One survey will be performed during the injection phase to confirm plume movement and direction.

rows.detail: Permanent solar-powered eddy covariance towers (CSAT3 sonic anemometer, LI-7500A open-path analyzer, 4-5 m) downwind of injection and monitoring wells; hourly CO2 concentration and flux via EddyPro, fed to the Central Control Center.
rows.location: One tower east (downwind) of each injection site
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomalous, rising CO2: test tower equipment, targeted point-source and soil gas investigation; leak mass computed from increased flux.
rows.evidence_quote: Broad aerial surface air monitoring will be conducted with permanently installed eddy covariance towers (Figure 10).

rows.detail: Equipment leaks and operational venting between the injection meter and wellhead estimated with GHGRP/Subpart W procedures (98.444(d)); event-driven engineering estimates for other surface leaks.
rows.location: Surface equipment between flow meter and wellhead
rows.evidence_quote: Monitoring efforts will evaluate and estimate leaks from equipment and vented CO2 as required under 40 CFR § 98.444(d).

rows.detail: Safety valve function testing: 'biannual' surface safety valve tests per API 6AV1 and annual master and wellhead isolation valve tests.
rows.trigger_or_response: Inoperable surface safety valve: shut in well immediately, repair within 90 days or set alternative schedule.
rows.evidence_quote: Biannual testing of surface safety valve systems will be conducted to ensure their ability to hold anticipated pressure.

rows.detail: Pipeline and facility instrumentation watched by 24/7 operations staff through SCADA with manual and automatic shutdowns; remote pipeline monitoring to spot leaks.
rows.location: Pipelines and facilities within the MMA
rows.trigger_or_response: Suspected leak assessed in field by visual inspection, gas analysis, and soil gas for buried pipelines.
rows.evidence_quote: Instrumentation will be installed on pipelines and facilities that allow the 24/7 operations staff to monitor the process and potentially spot leaks.

rows.detail: Surveillance of third-party drilling: WOGCC unitization order ensures notification of permits to drill through the caprock; High Plains also checks the WOGCC online data explorer.
rows.trigger_or_response: Third-party well through Lyons: coordinate wellbore monitoring with operator and add wellhead to surface monitoring if accessible.
rows.evidence_quote: High Plains will also assess potential drilling activity via the WOGCC online data explorer.

notes: Pages 9, 12, 13, 16-21, 26-30, 32, 38 and 39 are figure pages with no extracted text; Figure 10 (p32), which shows monitoring well, eddy covariance tower and soil gas locations, is image-only, so locations are known only from the text and Appendices A-B. Production_monitoring is recorded not_found because the plan states no CO2 is produced, entrained or recycled (p40). Reservoir_pressure is coded mentioned_only: the plan mentions 'downhole pressure and temperature measurements' for plume stabilization (p44) but never identifies injection-zone gauges; the M-1 gauges monitor the Sundance above the confining zone. DTS/DAS fiber behind casing in M-1 wells is described as installed or planned 'for future utility' (p34), i.e. not an active commitment beyond the annual DTS/temperature logs. 'Biannual' surface safety valve testing (p42) is ambiguous (twice yearly vs every two years); frequency row coded annual on the master valve test. The plan says six M-1 wells but only Juniper M-1 and Spirea M-1R fully penetrate the confining zone (p15). Point-source monitoring 'once per year at other locations' (p41) does not specify whether abandoned wells (Fritz 1, UPRR Palm 1-21, Cypress M-2) are included. MIT frequency is deferred to WDEQ Class VI permits. The Class VI permits are cited as governing the 2D seismic and groundwater protocols but are not reproduced.
